content.title: The Epistles of Ignatius
content.author: Ignatius of Antioch (d. c. 110) · Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885), tr. Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson
content.note: Letters written on the way to martyrdom in Rome, early in the second century. To the Ephesians 18–19 and To the Smyrnaeans 1 name Mary's virginity and Jesus' birth among the church's settled confession. Public domain translation; the held copy is CCEL's electronic text, so a long extract would be checked against a scan of the printed volume first.
content.read: Held in this project's corpus: CCEL's text export sources/library/source-patristic-ccel/anf01.txt. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 7): To the Ephesians 18–19 and To the Smyrnaeans 1 (the shorter recension) read for virgin-birth. Described, not quoted. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 7): To the Ephesians 18 also cited by jesus-claims; 'our God, Jesus Christ' quoted.

publicDomain.edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1, translated by Alexander Roberts and James Donaldson (1885)
publicDomain.basis: The held CCEL text of the 1885 American edition (Buffalo: Christian Literature, 1885): published before 1931, so public domain in the US; Roberts d. 1901, Donaldson d. 1915.
